acceptance_criteria: A interaction partial R-squared at least 0.005
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared above 0 on macro-window holdout rows
Net daily edge after the 0.10% round-trip taker cost is positive
spec.alternative_hypothesis: The lag-1 BTC coefficient for next-day ETH returns is larger inside macro windows than outside them (positive interaction), and lag-1 BTC explains a positive out-of-sample component of next-day ETH returns within macro-window rows.
spec.benchmark: Own-history baseline: next-bar ETH return predicted from its own lagged return, the SOL common factor and lag-1 BTC, with the interaction excluded
cost_assumptions: OKX VIP0 taker fee 0.05% per side, from the OKX public fee schedule (okx.com/fees), checked 2026-11-18; treated as an assumption, not verified for the user's account
Funding rate costs ignored; perpetual funding can exceed taker fees over holding periods
Slippage and market impact ignored; both would reduce any edge
spec.cost_model: Round-trip taker cost 0.10% per position flip (OKX VIP0 taker 0.05% per side, assumed); sign rule on out-of-sample augmented forecasts on macro-window holdout rows only, 1x, flat on non-window rows; entry from flat and final exit cost one taker side each; funding, slippage and market impact ignored
exclusions: Unconfirmed (forming) OKX bars are excluded; only confirm=1 candles enter the panel
The first daily return row has no lag-1 predictor and is excluded; the same warm-up rule applies to the 1H panel
Bars after the preregistered window end 2026-11-18T16:00Z are out of sample
The October 2025 CPI was never published, so no window bar exists for that reference month
known_confounders: The release content (whether the print surprised) is not known at t; this study tests the release-day effect, not the surprise effect, and must not be read as evidence about macro surprises or their transmission
A window effect must not be default-attributed to any mechanism (e.g. institutional rebalancing); the report writes only to 'consistent/inconsistent with ...'

The CPI calendar was transcribed from the BLS Schedule of Selected Releases pages via text fetch and cross-checked against the BLS archived releases page and second sources; BLS returns HTTP 403 to direct programmatic requests, so the calendar is not structured BLS API output. The October 2025 CPI was never published (2025 lapse in appropriations), so no event exists for that reference month.
Macro windows are scarce (about 20 events per year); the daily window sample is 116 rows of about 2,100, so power against small effects is limited
The SOL common-factor proxy is itself driven by BTC and may absorb part of the transmission effect; no-factor controls are reported as upper bounds
Common crypto market shocks move BTC, ETH and SOL together; the regressions control for the contemporaneous third-asset return only

The CPI window bar opened the day before the release date and the FOMC window bar opened on the statement day; both offsets are fixed by the release times against the 16:00 UTC bar open and are DST-independent
spec.mechanism: Scheduled macro releases concentrate information flow on release days, so price discovery in the largest market (BTC perpetuals) may transmit to ETH with a stronger lag inside the window. The window indicator is known at t (release schedules are public in advance), but the release content — whether the print surprised — is NOT known at t. This study tests the release-day effect, not the surprise effect, and does not claim to measure macro surprises or their transmission. A window effect must not be default-attributed to any mechanism (e.g. institutional rebalancing); the report writes only to 'consistent/inconsistent with ...' for any mechanism story.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count
model_definition: Interaction OLS with HAC standard errors (daily BTC→ETH, 1H BTC→ETH)
Macro-window-subsample partial lead-lag with HAC standard errors
Window-aware purged walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation (macro-window holdout rows only)
Macro-window counts over the preregistered sample (daily bars 2021-01-21..2026-11-16): 116 window bars (69 CPI, 47 FOMC), no in-sample overlap; the single overlap bar (2026-12-09) is out of sample
Wide-window (event bar ±1 bar), FOMC-only vs CPI-only and subperiod splits as descriptive checks (not in the test family)

Treasury auction-day splits are descriptive only, conditional on the auction calendar being verifiable from the U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data API (auctions_query) with a TreasuryDirect cross-check; if the calendar cannot be verified, the auction splits are omitted and the report says why. Auction days never enter the main window (FOMC + CPI only).
spec.multiple_testing_family: Macro-window BTC→ETH daily transmission (3 tests: A daily interaction, B daily macro-window subsample, C 1H interaction)
spec.null_hypothesis: Lag-1 BTC returns have no macro-window-dependent incremental predictive value: the interaction coefficient is zero and lag-1 BTC does not predict ETH returns within macro-window rows, beyond ETH's own history and the common-factor control, after costs and dependence controls.
spec.primary_metric: Partial R-squared of the BTC×macro-window interaction in the daily BTC→ETH interaction regression
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted A interaction p-value at or above 0.05
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared at or below 0 on macro-window holdout rows
Net daily edge after costs is zero or negative
spec.research_question: Does lag-1 BTC perpetual return predict the next-day ETH perpetual return more strongly inside macro windows (one OKX daily bar per FOMC statement / CPI release: the bar whose return interval contains the release moment) than outside them?
spec.target_definition: Next-day close-to-close ETH-USDT perpetual log return (daily primary); next-hour ETH-USDT perpetual log return (1H secondary)
spec.title: Macro windows strengthen BTC→ETH transmission
